shadow:
There is a hunger that never quite switches off. You eat and an hour later it is back. You finish a thing you wanted and the wanting moves on to the next thing without thanking you. This is older than any one life. It runs under food and money and praise and the next room you walk into.

The hunger itself is honest. It is the part of you that refuses to settle for a smaller life. The trouble starts only with where it gets pointed. Pointed outward, it sends you chasing the thing that promises to fill you, and the thing always half delivers, and you are left a little emptier than before you reached. Then comes the part most people get wrong. They decide the thing failed them, or the person did, and they go looking again. Or they cling to whatever briefly worked and call that clinging a life.

The way out is not less hunger. It is feeling the hunger fully enough to notice it is not a hole in you. It is an engine, and it has been driving in the wrong direction. Sit inside the wanting without grabbing. The grip starts to loosen on its own.
repressive: Some push the hunger down because they fear where it would take them. They keep it underground, and life flattens into boredom. They may not even name it boredom. The eyes go dull. Nothing tastes of much.
reactive: Others stay too busy to feel it. They fill every hour, chase the next stimulus, move from one bright thing to the next. They blame whatever they just left for not being enough. Little of it ever joins up into a life.
gift:
Something shifts when the hunger turns inward. It still wants, but it stops sending you out to ransack the world. It starts moving you closer to what is already near.

This is adventure, and it is smaller than the word sounds. Not crossing oceans. More like noticing that your days have quietly sorted themselves into sealed compartments. Work in one. The people you love in another. The thing you are curious about kept off to the side because there is no time. Adventure is opening a door between two of those rooms and letting them mix.

Learn the name of the man who sells you bread. Read the kind of book you would normally never pick up. Put food out for birds you cannot identify yet. None of it is grand. All of it is you reaching across a gap you had stopped noticing was a gap.

The hunger does not vanish here. You stop trying to kill it. You let it pull you toward closeness instead of conquest, and the closeness feeds something the conquest never could. There is still some fear in it. You go anyway. That is the whole move. You go, and the going changes you on the way.
siddhi:
Far enough in, the reaching stops. Not from getting full. The one who was hungry is simply not there to be hungry anymore. What is left has no edges.

This is boundlessness, and it cannot really be carried back into words. The heart, it turns out, was never a fenced thing. It was the part of you that always knew the universe had no walls, and the mind kept arguing otherwise. Here the argument ends. Love and consciousness become one word, because they always were.

From this place the laws bend. A child believes anything is possible and is not wrong, only early. The siddhi keeps that knowing and stops calling it innocence.

Look back down the whole road from here. The hunger at the start was not a defect in you. It was the homing signal. It ached because it remembered something boundless and would not let you forget. It drove you out, and out, and finally in. It was always pointing here.
